To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the effectiveness of disinfection against EBOV varies by matrix, 2) 5% peracidic acid was effective in reducing EBOV titres in blood on surfaces, 3) the effectiveness of other disinfectants against blood on surfaces was inconsistent, and 4) 5% hydrogen peroxide and 5% sodium hypochlorite were effective against EBOV on laboratory glassware and plastic.
5% peracid is effective against EBOV on surfaces in blood, while other disinfectants are less effective.
5% per acetic acid consistently reduced virus titers to the assay limit in dried blood, and that no disinfectant was consistently effective against EBOV on surfaces in blood or saliva matrices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, efficient and environmentally friendly methods of disinfection and sterilization of surfaces, medical instruments, medical devices, and medical products.
the development and evaluation of disinfectant efficacy of various disinfectants against Ebola Virus.
the evaluation of disinfectants in the laboratory and clinical matrices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5% peracid is the only disinfectant with a high probability of being effective against EBOV, and it is effective only in blood.
the disinfectants tested were ineffective against EBOV, and the only disinfectant that was consistently effective was the 5% peracid.
5% per acetic acid is the only disinfectant that is consistently effective against EBOV on surfaces in blood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficacy of disinfectants is highly dependent on the matrix in which they are used.
5% per acetic acid is the most effective disinfectant against EBOV, and the efficacy is consistent across different matrices and surface types.
the use of 5% peracid disinfectants is a promising approach to reduce EBOV titration in blood on surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disinfection of EBOV in clinical matrices remains challenging.
disinfectant effectiveness against EBOV is dependent on the matrix.
the use of disinfectants in clinical and laboratory settings is critical to prevent EBOV transmission.
